topics.label: Lecture introduction and cancer hallmarks overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's objectives, historical context of cancer hallmarks, and the progression model of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Growth factor independence and proliferative signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt, and TGF-beta cascades drive sustained cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in leukemia and solid tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how arrests in normal cell differentiation contribute to neoplastic transformation in hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Mechanisms of resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how alterations in the p53 pathway and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and stress-induced senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how telomere dynamics and stress signaling trigger senescence, how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality through telomerase reactivation, and summarize cell-autonomous growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and the Warburg effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring across tumor types, and the role of oncometabolites in altering the cancer epigenome.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and blood supply induction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how tumors switch on angiogenesis to satisfy oxygen and nutrient demands during malignant progression.

topics.label: Cancer invasion, dissemination, and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the metastatic cascade, factors governing secondary site colonization, and the clonal genetics underlying metastatic spread.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the convergence of cancer hallmarks and providing closing practical remarks.
